newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican Raul Salinas linked to businessmen-report.
newsitem.headline: Mexican Raul Salinas linked to businessmen-report.

text.p: Two prominent Mexican businessmen have been named as business partners of the jailed brother of ex-President Carlos Salinas de Gortari, Reforma newspaper said on Tuesday.

Reforma said new testimony in the case against Raul Salinas widened the circle of leading businessmen that allegedly worked in some way with Salinas, who is in jail on charges of murder, corruption and money laundering.
One of the men, David Penaloza, is head of one of the country's largest construction companies, Tribasa SA. He denied to Reforma ever knowingly working with Salinas.

Reforma said it obtained testimony from a former assistant to Salinas, Margarita Nava Sanchez, which claims Salinas set up a construction company under her name and an alias of Raul Salinas a few months after his brother came to power in 1988.

According to the testimony, Salinas helped his company obtain public works contracts and worked with Tribasa on part of a Mexico City-Toluca highway concession carried out during Carlos Salinas' 1988-1994 term. Reforma said officials suspect the company, Maramex SA, may have been used to help Salinas hide millions of dollars in ill-gotten gains.

Salinas' lawyer, Eduardo Luengo Creel, told Reforma the information in the testimony was correct. But Penaloza denied ever working with Salinas, who is being investigated by Swiss and Mexican officials for allegedly laundering more than $100 million in secret bank accounts in several countries.

"I know Raul Salinas ... I knew and dealt with him, but never had any business dealings with the man," Penaloza said. "We subcontracted a lot of people for smaller jobs on that concession ... I don't know if in one of those companies there appeared the name of this lady or of Raul ..."

The testimony also said Salinas set up another company, Citricos Mexicanos SA, with Enrique Regules Uriegas, a well-known businessman in Monterrey and, according to information from the Mexican Stock Exchange, a member of the board of directors of brokerage firm Abaco SA.

Several other leading Mexican businessmen including billionaire telecommunications magnate Carlos Peralta have admitted to doing business with Salinas. Peralta said he gave him $50 million for an investment fund that was later deposited in Switzerland and is under investigation.
